why: Both advisors make the right call. Advice 2 gives a more accurate cost analysis: the $98 discount only matters if the customer would have stayed 12 months anyway, and it breaks even at about 3% monthly churn. Advice 2 also covers practical issues Advice 1 misses, such as refund policy, annual invoicing needs, and delayed price increases. Advice 1 is more actionable, but its dated pass/fail thresholds (10 of 40 switching, cutting the discount for new signups) are arbitrary and presented with more confidence than the facts support.
